set1.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set1.q: A 67-year-old man with chronic left-sided heart failure now has right-sided failure as well. Which management approach is most appropriate?
opts: Start a calcium channel blocker
Calcium channel blockers are avoided in heart failure. Right-sided failure is treated as left-sided failure is, plus its cause.
Start home inotropic support
Inotropes are for intensive care use only. Right-sided failure is treated as left-sided failure is, plus its cause.
Treat as left-sided failure and its cause
Correct. Right-sided failure is treated the same as left-sided failure, with symptom management and treatment of the underlying cause, moving to transplant or palliative care as it advances.
Stop his left-sided heart failure drugs
Right-sided failure is treated the same as left-sided failure, so his guideline-directed therapy continues alongside treatment of the cause.

set1.io: Compare and contrast precipitating factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis (including role of B-type natriuretic peptide, BNP), and treatment of acute decompensated heart failure.
set1.q: A 73-year-old woman has grade II diastolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 46%. She has fatigue and breathlessness with exertion but has never had pulmonary or peripheral edema and has never needed a diuretic. Does she meet a clinical diagnosis of congestive heart failure?
opts: Yes, because she is older than 65
Age does not define the diagnosis. A clinical diagnosis of congestive heart failure requires congestion, meaning edema.
No, because congestion is required

Correct. A clinical diagnosis of congestive heart failure requires congestion, meaning pulmonary or peripheral edema. She has symptoms and a mildly reduced ejection fraction, but without edema the congestive label does not apply.
Yes, because she has symptoms
Symptoms make heart failure clinical, but calling it congestive requires congestion, meaning edema, which she has never had.
Yes, because her fraction is 46%
Her fraction places her in the mildly reduced group; it does not make the heart failure congestive. Congestion, meaning edema, is required.

set1.io: Define the following diagnostic and therapeutic groups of HF patients, and the treatment implications/recommendations for each group: a. HF with reduced EF (HFrEF) b. HF with mildly reduced EF (HFmrEF) c. HF with preserved EF (HFpEF)
set1.q: A 61-year-old man with reduced ejection fraction asks why his clinician raises one medicine at a time rather than starting everything at full strength. Which explanation is accurate?
opts: Therapy is optimized as tolerated
Correct. Guideline-directed therapy is prioritized for his comorbidities and optimized as hemodynamically stable, so each class is increased as blood pressure and tolerance allow.
Full doses are unsafe in any patient
The point is not a universal ban on full doses. Therapy is optimized as hemodynamically stable, increasing each class as tolerated.
Only one drug can be taken at once
Reduced ejection fraction uses several classes together. They are increased step by step as blood pressure and tolerance allow.
Medicines stop once symptoms go
Therapy aims to improve survival and slow progression as well as symptoms, so it continues. It is optimized as tolerated.

set1.io: Define the following diagnostic and therapeutic groups of HF patients, and the treatment implications/recommendations for each group: a. HF with reduced EF (HFrEF) b. HF with mildly reduced EF (HFmrEF) c. HF with preserved EF (HFpEF)
set1.q: A 59-year-old man with dilated cardiomyopathy has an ejection fraction of 25%, breathlessness with exertion and no symptoms at rest. He takes furosemide and sacubitril-valsartan. Which drug class should be added as core therapy?
opts: Hydralazine with isosorbide dinitrate
That pairing is for African American patients in functional class III or IV, added after the core classes. He still lacks the sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor

Correct. Reduced ejection fraction carries strong recommendations for a beta blocker, renin-angiotensin blockade, a mineralocorticoid antagonist and a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor; he has only the renin-angiotensin piece so far.
Calcium channel blocker such as diltiazem
Calcium channel blockers are avoided in heart failure. The missing core classes include the sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
Milrinone as an outpatient infusion
Milrinone is an inotrope reserved for the intensive care unit. The missing core classes include the sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.

set1.io: Define the following diagnostic and therapeutic groups of HF patients, and the treatment implications/recommendations for each group: a. HF with reduced EF (HFrEF) b. HF with mildly reduced EF (HFmrEF) c. HF with preserved EF (HFpEF)
set1.q: A 68-year-old woman has fatigue and breathlessness with exertion. Echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 45%, and her fraction has never been lower. Which heart failure group describes her?
opts: Improved ejection fraction
Improved ejection fraction needs an earlier value of 40% or less. Hers has never been lower, so she is mildly reduced.
Mildly reduced ejection fraction
Correct. 45% falls in the 41 to 49% band, and with no earlier value of 40% or less there is nothing to make it improved ejection fraction. Her treatment then resembles preserved ejection fraction.
Reduced ejection fraction
Reduced ejection fraction is 40% or less. At 45% she falls in the mildly reduced band.
Preserved ejection fraction
Preserved ejection fraction starts at 50%. At 45% she falls in the mildly reduced band.

set1.io: Define each class of the New York Heart Association (NYHA) symptomatic and functional classification of heart failure.
set1.q: A 71-year-old man with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction is comfortable at rest but becomes breathless after only a few steps across a room. Which New York Heart Association class describes him?
opts: Class III
Correct. Symptoms with only slight exertion, such as a few steps across a room, and none at rest are class III. Class II is symptoms with ordinary exertion and class IV is symptoms at rest.
Class II
Class II is symptoms with ordinary exertion. Breathlessness after only slight effort, like a few steps across a room, is class III.
Class IV
Class IV is symptoms at rest, and he is comfortable at rest. Slight exertion provoking symptoms is class III.
Class I
Class I is the absence of any heart failure symptoms. Breathlessness with only slight exertion is class III.

set1.io: Define the following diagnostic and therapeutic groups of HF patients, and the treatment implications/recommendations for each group: a. HF with reduced EF (HFrEF) b. HF with mildly reduced EF (HFmrEF) c. HF with preserved EF (HFpEF)
set1.q: A 77-year-old man with preserved ejection fraction heart failure (fraction 58%) is euvolemic on a loop diuretic. He has no diabetes. Which drug class is the next best-supported addition?
opts: Angiotensin II receptor blocker alone
The receptor blocker is a weak recommendation in preserved ejection fraction. The sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor is better supported.
Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor

Correct. In preserved ejection fraction, after diuretics as needed, the sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor carries a moderate recommendation, stronger than the weak ones for the neprilysin combination, antagonist and receptor blocker.
Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist
The antagonist is only a weak recommendation in preserved ejection fraction. The sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor is better supported.
Calcium channel blocker such as diltiazem
Calcium channel blockers are avoided in heart failure. The next best-supported class is the sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.

set1.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set1.q: A 69-year-old woman with reduced ejection fraction (fraction 27%) has blood pressure above goal on her heart failure regimen. Verapamil is proposed. What is the most appropriate response?
opts: Add it once she reaches class IV
Advancing class does not make calcium channel blockers appropriate. They are avoided in heart failure at every class.
Avoid it and use recommended classes
Correct. Verapamil is a calcium channel blocker, and calcium channel blockers are avoided in heart failure. Pressure control comes from optimizing the recommended classes as tolerated.
Start it as first-line pressure control
Calcium channel blockers are not first-line in heart failure; they are avoided. The recommended classes are optimized instead.
Use it in place of her beta blocker
Replacing a core beta blocker with a calcium channel blocker is backwards; the calcium channel blocker is avoided in heart failure.

set1.io: Differentiate each stage of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA), natural history classification of heart failure, and associated treatment recommendations of each stage.
set1.q: A 56-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, obesity and a normal echocardiogram has no symptoms. His clinician plans to start metoprolol to prevent heart failure. Which drug class should not be chosen first here?
opts: A sodium-glucose drug such as empagliflozin
Empagliflozin is a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, exactly the recommended first drug in stage A with diabetes. The class not to choose first is the beta blocker.
Lifestyle risk factor control
Controlling risk factors such as obesity belongs with stage A care and is not the problem here. The class not to choose first is the beta blocker.
Glucose-lowering therapy in general
Treating his diabetes is appropriate, and the preferred drug class itself lowers glucose. The class not to choose first is the beta blocker.
A beta blocker

Correct. He is stage A, at risk with a normal heart, and the first drug for an at-risk patient with diabetes is a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor. The beta blocker is a stage B therapy once structural disease exists.

set1.io: Compare and contrast precipitating factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis (including role of B-type natriuretic peptide, BNP), and treatment of acute decompensated heart failure.
set1.q: A 73-year-old woman with chronic heart failure has a B-type natriuretic peptide that has risen by 100 since her last visit. What does this change imply?
opts: About 5% higher relative risk of death
That understates it. Each rise of 100 carries about a 35% increase in the relative risk of death.
About 90% higher relative risk of death
That overstates it. Each rise of 100 carries about a 35% increase in the relative risk of death.
No change in her relative risk of death
The level carries prognostic weight: each rise of 100 adds about 35% to the relative risk of death.
About 35% higher relative risk of death
Correct. Each increase of 100 carries about a 35% increase in the relative risk of death, so a rising level is a warning sign even when symptoms seem stable.

set1.io: Differentiate between systolic dysfunction and diastolic dysfunction..
set1.q: A 58-year-old man with known dilated cardiomyopathy has worsening breathlessness. Blood pressure is 102/64, a third heart sound (an extra sound in early diastole just after the second heart sound) is present, and he has crackles. Which ejection fraction is the echocardiogram expected to show?
opts: About 45%
45% is mildly reduced, between the two chains. Dilated cardiomyopathy with a third sound and low pressure fits a clearly reduced value near 25%.
About 75%
A high value is the opposite of a failing squeeze. Dilated cardiomyopathy with a third sound fits a reduced ejection fraction near 25%.
About 25%

Correct. Dilated cardiomyopathy is the systolic chain: poor contraction, a reduced ejection fraction of 40% or less, low-normal pressure, a third heart sound and pulmonary edema. A value near 25% fits.
About 60%
A preserved ejection fraction belongs to the diastolic chain of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Dilated cardiomyopathy with these signs gives a reduced value near 25%.

set1.io: Compare and contrast precipitating factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis (including role of B-type natriuretic peptide, BNP), and treatment of acute decompensated heart failure.
set1.q: A 58-year-old man had an anterior myocardial infarction one week ago with acute heart failure. Echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 30%. He is now stable. Which is the most appropriate next step for protection against sudden death?
opts: Home inotropes until the heart recovers
Inotropes are for intensive care use only. The first step is a wearable defibrillator while therapy is optimized.
Wearable defibrillator while therapy is optimized

Correct. After acute heart failure from infarction with an ejection fraction below 35%, the pathway is a wearable defibrillator vest, optimized guideline-directed therapy with cardiac rehabilitation, a repeat echocardiogram, and an implantable device only if there is no improvement.
Implantable defibrillator before discharge
The implantable device comes last, only if a repeat echocardiogram after optimized therapy shows no improvement. The first step is a wearable defibrillator.
No protection until a repeat echo in a year
Leaving him unprotected ignores the risk; about half of cardiac arrests in these patients are ventricular arrhythmias. A wearable defibrillator comes first.

set1.io: Compare and contrast precipitating factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis (including role of B-type natriuretic peptide, BNP), and treatment of acute decompensated heart failure.
set1.q: A 67-year-old woman takes sacubitril-valsartan for reduced ejection fraction. Which natriuretic peptide result should not be relied on to judge her congestion?
opts: B-type natriuretic peptide
Correct. Neprilysin degrades B-type natriuretic peptide, so blocking neprilysin with sacubitril alters that level. The N-terminal fragment is the one to rely on.
N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide
The N-terminal fragment is not the peptide tied to neprilysin degradation. The unreliable result on this drug is B-type natriuretic peptide.
Either peptide, since both are altered
Only B-type natriuretic peptide is degraded by neprilysin. The N-terminal fragment remains usable.
Neither peptide, since neither is altered
The drug does alter one of them: B-type natriuretic peptide, which neprilysin degrades.

set1.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set1.q: A 44-year-old woman has weight loss, tremor, heat intolerance and palpitations for two months, and now ankle edema and breathlessness. Heart rate is 124 and B-type natriuretic peptide is elevated. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Right-sided failure from mitral stenosis
Mitral stenosis gives a diastolic rumble with an opening snap, not a hyperthyroid picture. This is high-output failure from hyperthyroidism.
High-output failure from hyperthyroidism

Correct. Hyperthyroidism raises peripheral demand, and the heart answers with a faster rate and stronger contraction until the heart failure syndrome appears: fatigue, dyspnea, edema and palpitations.
Systolic failure from ischemic disease
Nothing suggests infarction or ischemia, and the thyroid picture explains increased demand. This is high-output failure from hyperthyroidism.
Diastolic failure from hypertension
She has no long hypertension or fourth sound. The weight loss, tremor and heat intolerance point to high-output failure from hyperthyroidism.

set1.io: Differentiate each stage of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA), natural history classification of heart failure, and associated treatment recommendations of each stage.
set1.q: A 52-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and hypertension has no cardiac symptoms. Her echocardiogram is normal. Which drug class is recommended first to lower her risk of heart failure?
opts: Beta blocker as the first agent
A beta blocker is a stage B therapy, added once structural disease exists. In stage A with diabetes the first drug is a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist
The antagonist belongs to symptomatic heart failure, strongly in reduced ejection fraction. Stage A with diabetes calls for a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
Loop diuretic such as bumetanide
A loop diuretic treats congestion, which she does not have. Stage A with diabetes calls for a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor

Correct. Risk factors with a normal heart and no symptoms are stage A, at risk for heart failure, and the one strong drug recommendation there is a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor in patients with diabetes, not a beta blocker.

set1.io: Define the following diagnostic and therapeutic groups of HF patients, and the treatment implications/recommendations for each group: a. HF with reduced EF (HFrEF) b. HF with mildly reduced EF (HFmrEF) c. HF with preserved EF (HFpEF)
set1.q: A 74-year-old woman with long-standing hypertension has leg edema, crackles and breathlessness climbing stairs. Echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 62% and B-type natriuretic peptide is 640. Which therapy carries the strongest recommendation now?
opts: An inotrope such as dobutamine
Inotropes are for intensive care use only. With preserved fraction and congestion, the strong recommendation is a diuretic as needed.
A diuretic as needed for congestion

Correct. With preserved ejection fraction and congestion, diuretics as needed carry the strong recommendation. A sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor is next at moderate strength; the neprilysin combination, antagonist and receptor blocker are weak.
A beta blocker titrated to heart rate
A beta blocker is core therapy in reduced ejection fraction, not the strongest recommendation with a preserved fraction. Her congestion is treated with a diuretic as needed.
Hydralazine with isosorbide dinitrate
That pairing is for African American patients with reduced ejection fraction in functional class III or IV. With preserved fraction and congestion, the strong recommendation is a diuretic.

set1.io: Compare and contrast precipitating factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis (including role of B-type natriuretic peptide, BNP), and treatment of acute decompensated heart failure.
set1.q: A 59-year-old man is recovering from acute heart failure after an infarction with an ejection fraction of 29%. He wears a defibrillator vest while his guideline-directed therapy is being optimized. Which referral should accompany this phase?
opts: Hospice enrollment
Hospice does not fit a recovery pathway that ends in a repeat echocardiogram. The referral that accompanies this phase is cardiac rehabilitation.
Transplant evaluation
Transplant is for failure that progresses despite management. The referral that accompanies this phase is cardiac rehabilitation.
Valve surgery review
Nothing points to valve disease. The referral that accompanies optimized therapy after acute failure is cardiac rehabilitation.
Cardiac rehabilitation

Correct. After acute heart failure with an ejection fraction below 35%, the pathway pairs optimized guideline-directed therapy with cardiac rehabilitation while he wears the vest, before the echocardiogram is repeated.

set1.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set1.q: A 66-year-old man presents for the first time with breathlessness, leg edema, crackles and a B-type natriuretic peptide of 720. Which is the most appropriate next step to classify his heart failure?
opts: Echocardiogram

Correct. Signs, symptoms and an elevated peptide support a clinical diagnosis, and the echocardiogram then shows structure most accurately and sorts him into an ejection fraction group, which decides therapy.
Right heart catheterization
Catheterization grades hemodynamic severity in selected right-sided failure. Classification by ejection fraction and structure starts with an echocardiogram.
Repeat the peptide next week
Repeating the peptide will not classify him. The echocardiogram defines structure and ejection fraction group.
Exercise stress testing
Stress testing does not classify heart failure. The echocardiogram defines structure and ejection fraction group.

set1.io: Compare and contrast precipitating factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis (including role of B-type natriuretic peptide, BNP), and treatment of acute decompensated heart failure.
set1.q: A 55-year-old woman has breathlessness on exertion for a week. Her B-type natriuretic peptide is 45. Which is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Look for a non-cardiac cause
Correct. A level below 100 rules out acute heart failure with a negative predictive value above 90%, so her breathlessness needs another explanation.
Start a loop diuretic today
A diuretic treats congestion from heart failure, which a level of 45 rules out acutely. Another cause should be sought.
Admit for acute heart failure
Acute heart failure is likely only above 900. At 45 it is ruled out, and another cause should be sought.
Order an implantable device
A defibrillator requires established reduced ejection fraction and other criteria. At 45 acute heart failure is ruled out.

set1.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set1.q: A 72-year-old woman with heart failure asks why she must take several medicines when she already feels better. Which explanation matches the goals of treatment?
opts: They are meant to cure her cardiomyopathy
Cure is not among the treatment goals. The goals are fewer symptoms, longer survival and slower progression.
They are meant to make her ejection fraction normal
A normal ejection fraction is not a goal of treatment. The goals are fewer symptoms, longer survival and slower progression.
They also extend life and slow progression
Correct. The goals are to decrease symptoms, increase survival and limit disease progression. Feeling better meets only the first of the three, so the regimen continues.
They are only needed while she has symptoms
Symptom relief is one goal among three. Increasing survival and limiting progression continue after she feels better.

set1.io: Differentiate each stage of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA), natural history classification of heart failure, and associated treatment recommendations of each stage.
set1.q: A 59-year-old woman in stage B, pre-heart failure, developed side effects on lisinopril and could not tolerate it. Which is the recommended alternative?
opts: Sacubitril-valsartan combination
The neprilysin combination is recommended for symptomatic reduced ejection fraction in functional class II or III, not stage B. The alternative is a receptor blocker.
Verapamil for blood pressure
Verapamil is a calcium channel blocker, avoided in heart failure. The stage B alternative is an angiotensin receptor blocker such as losartan.
Losartan, an angiotensin receptor blocker
Correct. Stage B lists an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor with an angiotensin receptor blocker if the inhibitor is not tolerated, alongside a beta blocker.
Stopping renin-angiotensin therapy
Intolerance of one agent does not end renin-angiotensin therapy. Stage B switches to an angiotensin receptor blocker such as losartan.

set1.io: Compare and contrast precipitating factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis (including role of B-type natriuretic peptide, BNP), and treatment of acute decompensated heart failure.
set1.q: A 67-year-old woman with heart failure has cool, clammy extremities, a narrow pulse pressure and sleepiness, along with orthopnea (breathlessness lying flat) and leg edema. Which bedside hemodynamic profile fits?
opts: Cold and wet
Correct. Low-perfusion signs (cool extremities, narrow pulse pressure, obtundation) plus congestion signs (orthopnea, edema) place her in the cold and wet profile, hypoperfusion with congestion.
Warm and wet
Warm and wet is congestion with adequate perfusion. Her cool extremities, narrow pulse pressure and sleepiness mean perfusion is low, so she is cold and wet.
Cold and dry
Cold and dry is low perfusion without congestion. Her orthopnea and edema mean she is congested, so she is cold and wet.
Warm and dry
Warm and dry is the normal profile. She has both low perfusion and congestion, so she is cold and wet.

set1.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set1.q: A 60-year-old man is newly diagnosed with heart failure and will start a loop diuretic. Which laboratory panel should be checked before starting?
opts: Thyroid function panel
Thyroid testing is not the pre-diuretic check. Potassium and renal function come from the complete metabolic panel.
Hepatic function panel
Liver tests are not what the diuretic calls for. Potassium and renal function come from the complete metabolic panel.
Coagulation panel
Clotting tests are not the pre-diuretic check. Potassium and renal function come from the complete metabolic panel.
Complete metabolic panel
Correct. The metabolic panel gives potassium and renal function (blood urea nitrogen, creatinine and filtration rate), both of which a potassium-wasting loop diuretic affects.

set1.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set1.q: A 63-year-old woman has right-sided heart failure confirmed by echocardiogram. Her team now wants to know how hemodynamically severe it is. Which is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Chest radiograph series
A radiograph shows effusions and heart size but not hemodynamics. Severity is measured by right heart catheterization.
Troponin trend over a day
Troponin addresses infarction or ischemic cardiomyopathy. Severity is measured by right heart catheterization.
Right heart catheterization
Correct. Once right-sided failure is established, right heart catheterization measures its hemodynamic severity. The echocardiogram has already made the diagnosis.
Repeat echocardiogram
The echocardiogram made the diagnosis by ejection fraction. Hemodynamic severity is measured by right heart catheterization.

set1.io: Define the following diagnostic and therapeutic groups of HF patients, and the treatment implications/recommendations for each group: a. HF with reduced EF (HFrEF) b. HF with mildly reduced EF (HFmrEF) c. HF with preserved EF (HFpEF)
set1.q: A 66-year-old woman with reduced ejection fraction (fraction 30%) has gained weight with leg edema and crackles. She takes a beta blocker, sacubitril-valsartan, spironolactone and dapagliflozin. Which drug relieves her fluid overload now?
opts: Dobutamine given at home
Dobutamine is an inotrope for intensive care use only. Her congestion needs a loop diuretic.
Hydralazine given on its own
Hydralazine is paired with isosorbide dinitrate for selected patients in functional class III or IV; it does not clear fluid. Her congestion needs a loop diuretic.
A loop diuretic such as furosemide
Correct. Diuretics are used as needed for congestion in every ejection fraction group; loops such as furosemide and bumetanide are the potassium-wasting diuretics that clear fluid.
Diltiazem to slow the heart rate
Diltiazem is a calcium channel blocker, which is avoided in heart failure. Her congestion needs a loop diuretic.

set1.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set1.q: A 70-year-old man with heart failure and congestion is started on furosemide. Which counseling point is most appropriate?
opts: Potassium and kidney labs will be checked
Correct. Furosemide is a potassium-wasting loop diuretic, so potassium and renal function are followed on the complete metabolic panel.
His liver enzymes will be checked weekly
Liver tests are not the monitoring a loop diuretic needs. Potassium and renal function are followed on the metabolic panel.
It will raise his potassium to high levels
Loop diuretics waste potassium rather than raising it; it is the mineralocorticoid antagonists that spare it. Potassium and renal function will be checked.
No blood tests are needed on this drug
Monitoring is needed. Furosemide wastes potassium, so potassium and renal function are followed on the metabolic panel.

set1.io: Identify medical care strategies for heart failure in the lecture topic list for the following populations. 1. infant 2. child 3. adolescent 4. adult 5. elderly
set1.q: A 45-year-old man has two days of breathlessness after a viral illness. His N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide is 90. How should the result be read?
opts: Heart failure is likely
Younger than 75, heart failure becomes likely above 125. A level of 90 rules out acute failure.
Acute heart failure is likely
Nothing near this level suggests acute failure. Below 300 the N-terminal fragment rules it out.
The result is indeterminate
At 90 the result is clearly below the rule-out level of 300. Acute heart failure is ruled out.
Acute heart failure is ruled out
Correct. An N-terminal fragment below 300 rules out acute heart failure with a negative predictive value above 90%, and 90 is also below the under-75 heart failure threshold of 125.

set1.io: Differentiate between systolic dysfunction and diastolic dysfunction..
set1.q: A 64-year-old man with a myocardial infarction three years ago has breathlessness on exertion and orthopnea (breathlessness lying flat). Blood pressure is 104/68. There is a third heart sound (an extra sound in early diastole just after the second heart sound) and bibasilar crackles. B-type natriuretic peptide is 820. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Diastolic failure from hypertrophic disease
The diastolic chain runs with hypertension, a fourth heart sound and edema that starts peripherally. His low pressure, third sound and prior infarction point to systolic failure.
High-output failure from increased demand
High-output failure comes from anemia, hyperthyroidism or an arteriovenous fistula, with no infarction behind it. This is systolic failure from ischemic cardiomyopathy.
Isolated right-sided failure from the lungs
Right-sided failure shows peripheral edema, distended neck veins and portal overload. Crackles, orthopnea and a third sound point to left-sided systolic failure.
Systolic failure from ischemic cardiomyopathy

Correct. Every link of the systolic chain is here: ischemic cardiomyopathy after infarction, a low-normal blood pressure, a third heart sound from rapid filling of a dilated ventricle, and pulmonary edema, confirmed by an elevated natriuretic peptide.

set1.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set1.q: A 64-year-old man has combined right and left heart failure with symptoms at rest despite optimized guideline-directed therapy. Which course is most appropriate to discuss?
opts: Continuing dobutamine at home
Inotropes are for intensive care use only. Combined failure beyond optimized therapy points to transplant evaluation or comfort care.
Stopping all medicines and observing
Abandoning symptom control is not the plan. Combined failure beyond optimized therapy points to transplant evaluation or comfort care.
Transplant evaluation or comfort care
Correct. Combined right and left failure is managed with symptom control, comfort care and heart transplant. When optimized therapy no longer controls symptoms, those are the options to raise.
Adding a calcium channel blocker
Calcium channel blockers are avoided in heart failure. Combined failure beyond optimized therapy points to transplant evaluation or comfort care.

set1.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set1.q: A 76-year-old man with heart failure has cool extremities, a narrow pulse pressure and increasing confusion. His urine output has fallen and creatinine has doubled. Which complication has developed?
opts: Acute kidney injury from low perfusion
Correct. Cool extremities, narrow pulse pressure and obtundation are signs of low perfusion, and renal dysfunction with acute kidney injury and falling urine output is part of the same picture.
Nephrotic syndrome from proteinuria
Nephrotic syndrome is a primary kidney disorder. His low perfusion signs explain acute kidney injury with falling urine output.
Urinary retention from prostatic disease
Nothing points to an obstructed outlet, and the perfusion signs explain the kidneys. This is acute kidney injury from low perfusion.
Hypertensive kidney damage from years
Chronic hypertensive damage does not appear over days with cool extremities. This is acute kidney injury from low perfusion.

set2.io: Compare and contrast precipitating factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis (including role of B-type natriuretic peptide, BNP), and treatment of acute decompensated heart failure.
set2.q: An 80-year-old man in the intensive care unit with acute heart failure has cool extremities and hypotension, and inotropic support is being considered. Which agents are used for this?
opts: Spironolactone or eplerenone
These are mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists for chronic reduced ejection fraction. Inotropic support uses dobutamine or milrinone.
Losartan or irbesartan
These are angiotensin receptor blockers for chronic therapy. Inotropic support in intensive care uses dobutamine or milrinone.
Dobutamine or milrinone
Correct. Inotropic therapy for intensive care use includes the sympathomimetics dobutamine, norepinephrine and epinephrine and the phosphodiesterase inhibitor milrinone.
Diltiazem or verapamil
These are calcium channel blockers, which are avoided in heart failure. Inotropic support uses dobutamine or milrinone.

set2.io: Define the following diagnostic and therapeutic groups of HF patients, and the treatment implications/recommendations for each group: a. HF with reduced EF (HFrEF) b. HF with mildly reduced EF (HFmrEF) c. HF with preserved EF (HFpEF)
set2.q: A 57-year-old man had an ejection fraction of 25% two years ago. On guideline-directed therapy his repeat echocardiogram now shows 46%. How is his heart failure now classified?
opts: Improved ejection fraction
Correct. A fraction that was 40% or less and has recovered above 40% is improved ejection fraction. The number alone would read mildly reduced, but his history is what defines the group.
Mildly reduced ejection fraction
46% alone would be mildly reduced, but his earlier 25% changes the label. Recovery from the reduced range above 40% is improved ejection fraction.
Preserved ejection fraction
Preserved ejection fraction is 50% or more, which he has not reached. Recovery above 40% from a reduced value is improved ejection fraction.
Resolved heart failure
Heart failure is not relabeled as resolved when the fraction recovers. Recovery above 40% from 25% is improved ejection fraction.

set2.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set2.q: A 46-year-old woman with high-output heart failure from untreated hyperthyroidism has leg edema and breathlessness. Which treatment approach is most appropriate?
opts: Start verapamil to slow the heart rate
Verapamil is a calcium channel blocker, avoided in heart failure. The approach is to treat the cause and add a diuretic.
Refer for heart transplant evaluation
Transplant does not address a problem of excess demand. The approach is to treat the thyroid disease and add a diuretic.
Treat the thyroid disease and add a diuretic
Correct. High-output failure is treated by correcting the underlying cause of increased demand, here hyperthyroidism, with a diuretic for congestion.
Start dobutamine to support contractility
Dobutamine raises output further and is an inotrope for intensive care use only. The approach is to treat the cause and add a diuretic.

set2.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set2.q: A 62-year-old woman with long-standing hypertension has exertional breathlessness. Her electrocardiogram shows tall R waves in V5 and V6 and deep S waves in V1 and V2. What does this pattern show?
opts: Right heart strain
Right heart strain shows right axis deviation, right bundle branch block and T-wave inversions in V1 to V3. Her pattern is left ventricular hypertrophy.
Acute inferior injury
Acute injury shows ischemic changes such as elevation in the inferior leads. Her voltage pattern is left ventricular hypertrophy.
A normal tracing
Tall lateral R waves with deep right precordial S waves are abnormal; they indicate left ventricular hypertrophy.
Left ventricular hypertrophy
Correct. Tall R waves in V5 and V6 with deep S waves in V1 and V2 indicate left ventricular hypertrophy, the structural change behind hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and the diastolic chain.

set2.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set2.q: A 58-year-old man has leg edema and jugular venous distension (distended neck veins) with a raised B-type natriuretic peptide. Right-sided heart failure is suspected. Which test establishes the definitive diagnosis?
opts: Repeat natriuretic peptide
The peptide supports heart failure but cannot say which ventricle has failed. The echocardiogram gives the definitive diagnosis.
Twelve-lead electrocardiogram
The electrocardiogram may show right heart strain but does not make the diagnosis. The echocardiogram does.
Echocardiogram
Correct. Clinical heart failure with distended neck veins raises suspicion of right-sided failure, and the echocardiogram gives the definitive diagnosis by ejection fraction.
Right heart catheterization
Catheterization measures hemodynamic severity once right-sided failure is suspected or confirmed. The definitive diagnosis comes from the echocardiogram.

set2.io: Compare and contrast precipitating factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis (including role of B-type natriuretic peptide, BNP), and treatment of acute decompensated heart failure.
set2.q: A 64-year-old man with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction takes sacubitril-valsartan. He now has increasing breathlessness, and a natriuretic peptide test is planned. Which test is the more dependable choice?
opts: The N-terminal precursor fragment

Correct. The N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide is the choice: neprilysin degrades B-type natriuretic peptide, so an angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor alters that result. Knowing which peptide was measured matters in these patients.
B-type natriuretic peptide
Neprilysin degrades B-type natriuretic peptide, and sacubitril blocks neprilysin, so that result is altered. The N-terminal fragment is the more dependable choice.
Cardiac troponin level
Troponin addresses infarction or ischemic cardiomyopathy, not congestion. The more dependable natriuretic test here is the N-terminal fragment.
Complete blood count
The blood count helps the differential diagnosis but is not a natriuretic peptide. The N-terminal fragment is the dependable choice on this drug.

set2.io: Compare and contrast precipitating factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis (including role of B-type natriuretic peptide, BNP), and treatment of acute decompensated heart failure.
set2.q: A 72-year-old man comes to urgent care with two days of breathlessness. His B-type natriuretic peptide is 60. How should this result be interpreted?
opts: Acute heart failure is ruled out
Correct. A level below 100 rules out acute heart failure with a negative predictive value above 90%, so another cause of his breathlessness should be sought.
Heart failure is likely
Heart failure becomes likely only above 400. A level of 60 rules out acute heart failure.
The result is indeterminate
The indeterminate range is 100 to 400. At 60 the level rules out acute heart failure.
Acute heart failure is likely
Acute heart failure becomes likely only above 900. A level of 60 rules acute heart failure out.

set2.io: Identify medical care strategies for heart failure in the lecture topic list for the following populations. 1. infant 2. child 3. adolescent 4. adult 5. elderly
set2.q: An 81-year-old woman has progressive breathlessness and ankle edema over three months. Her N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide is 720. What does this level suggest for her age?
opts: Heart failure is likely
Correct. Older than 75, an N-terminal fragment above 450 makes heart failure likely. In a younger patient the threshold would be 125.
Heart failure is ruled out
No rule-out applies at 720. Older than 75, a level above 450 makes heart failure likely.
The level is normal for her age
The age-adjusted threshold over 75 is 450, and 720 exceeds it. Heart failure is likely.
Only a younger cut-off applies
The age-specific threshold exists precisely for patients older than 75: above 450 heart failure is likely.

set2.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set2.q: A 78-year-old woman with chronic heart failure has increasing lethargy, episodes of near-syncope and cool extremities, without new edema. Which feature of the heart failure syndrome do these findings reflect?
opts: Worsening pulmonary congestion
Congestion shows as orthopnea, crackles and edema, which she lacks. Lethargy, near-syncope and cool extremities reflect inadequate perfusion.
Portal venous overload
Portal overload gives nausea, poor appetite and an enlarged liver. Her findings reflect inadequate perfusion.
Systemic volume overload
Systemic overload shows as edema and distended neck veins, which she lacks. Her findings reflect inadequate perfusion.
Inadequate tissue perfusion
Correct. Weakness, fatigue, lethargy, malaise, syncope or near-syncope and obtundation are signs of inadequate tissue perfusion, the low-output side of the syndrome, distinct from congestion.

set2.io: Define the following diagnostic and therapeutic groups of HF patients, and the treatment implications/recommendations for each group: a. HF with reduced EF (HFrEF) b. HF with mildly reduced EF (HFmrEF) c. HF with preserved EF (HFpEF)
set2.q: A 63-year-old man with mildly reduced ejection fraction (fraction 44%) has ankle edema and breathlessness. Which therapy carries the strongest recommendation?
opts: A diuretic as needed

Correct. In mildly reduced ejection fraction, diuretics as needed carry the one strong recommendation. The sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor is moderate; the beta blocker, antagonist and renin-angiotensin drugs are weak.
An evidence-based beta blocker
In mildly reduced ejection fraction the beta blocker is a weak recommendation. The strongest is a diuretic as needed for his congestion.
A mineralocorticoid antagonist
The antagonist is a weak recommendation in mildly reduced ejection fraction. A diuretic as needed carries the strongest one.
A neprilysin combination drug
The angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor is weak in mildly reduced ejection fraction. A diuretic as needed carries the strongest recommendation.

set2.io: Define the following diagnostic and therapeutic groups of HF patients, and the treatment implications/recommendations for each group: a. HF with reduced EF (HFrEF) b. HF with mildly reduced EF (HFmrEF) c. HF with preserved EF (HFpEF)
set2.q: A 66-year-old African American man with reduced ejection fraction (fraction 25%) remains short of breath with slight exertion despite optimized sacubitril-valsartan, a beta blocker, spironolactone and dapagliflozin. Which addition is recommended?
opts: Hydralazine with isosorbide dinitrate

Correct. For African American patients with reduced ejection fraction in functional class III or IV, hydralazine with nitrates carries a strong recommendation on top of the core classes. Slight-exertion symptoms put him in functional class III.
Verapamil for additional rate control
Verapamil is a calcium channel blocker, which is avoided in heart failure. His class III disease qualifies for hydralazine with isosorbide dinitrate.
Isosorbide mononitrate on its own
The recommendation pairs hydralazine with isosorbide dinitrate. A nitrate alone is not the recommended addition for class III or IV.
Dobutamine continued at home
Dobutamine is an inotrope for intensive care use only. The recommended outpatient addition is hydralazine with isosorbide dinitrate.

set2.io: Differentiate each stage of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA), natural history classification of heart failure, and associated treatment recommendations of each stage.
set2.q: A 68-year-old woman was hospitalized last year for heart failure with edema. On treatment she is now symptom-free and asks whether she has moved back to stage B. Which reply is accurate?
opts: She remains in stage C
Correct. Stage C is symptomatic structural heart disease, past or current. Once symptoms have occurred, resolution on treatment does not move the stage backward.
She is now in stage B
Stage B is structural disease that has never caused symptoms. Her past symptoms keep her in stage C.
She is now in stage A
Stage A requires a structurally normal heart and no symptoms ever. She remains in stage C.
She has moved to stage D
Stage D is advanced heart failure, which her improvement does not suggest. She remains in stage C.

set2.io: Compare and contrast precipitating factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis (including role of B-type natriuretic peptide, BNP), and treatment of acute decompensated heart failure.
set2.q: A 60-year-old woman wore a defibrillator vest for three months after an infarction, with optimized guideline-directed therapy and cardiac rehabilitation. Her repeat echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 28%. She is class II and expected to live many years. Which is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Continue the vest indefinitely
The vest bridges the recovery period. With no improvement on the repeat echocardiogram, the next step is an implantable defibrillator.
Heart transplant evaluation now
Transplant is reserved for failure that cannot be controlled. She is class II and meets the criteria for an implantable defibrillator.
Stop therapy and recheck in a year
Stopping therapy would undo the optimization. With no improvement, the next step is an implantable defibrillator.
Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator

Correct. The pathway ends with an implantable device when the repeat echocardiogram shows no improvement. She also meets the criteria: ejection fraction 35% or less, class II or III, optimal therapy and life expectancy of at least one year.

set2.io: Differentiate between systolic dysfunction and diastolic dysfunction..
set2.q: A 71-year-old woman with 20 years of poorly controlled hypertension has ankle swelling that has recently spread to crackles at both lung bases. Blood pressure is 176/98. A fourth heart sound (a sound in late diastole just before the first heart sound) is heard. Echocardiogram shows thick left ventricular walls with an ejection fraction of 62%. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Systolic failure from dilated cardiomyopathy
Dilated cardiomyopathy gives a weak squeeze, a reduced ejection fraction, a normal or low pressure and a third sound. Her findings are the diastolic chain.
Systolic failure from ischemic cardiomyopathy
Ischemic cardiomyopathy leads the systolic chain with a reduced ejection fraction and low-normal pressure. Her hypertension, fourth sound and preserved fraction are diastolic.
High-output failure from thyroid excess
Hyperthyroid high-output failure brings tachycardia and palpitations from increased demand. Her long hypertension and fourth sound point to diastolic failure.
Diastolic failure from hypertrophic disease

Correct. The diastolic chain is complete: hypertension driving hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, a fourth heart sound from atrial contraction against a stiff ventricle, peripheral then pulmonary edema, and a preserved ejection fraction.

set2.io: Differentiate each stage of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA), natural history classification of heart failure, and associated treatment recommendations of each stage.
set2.q: A 60-year-old man with hypertension has never had cardiac symptoms. An echocardiogram shows left ventricular hypertrophy with preserved function. Which heart failure stage is he in?
opts: Stage D
Stage D is advanced heart failure. Asymptomatic hypertrophy is stage B, pre-heart failure.
Stage B
Correct. Asymptomatic structural heart disease, including left ventricular hypertrophy, is stage B, pre-heart failure. Stage A requires a structurally normal heart.
Stage A
Stage A is risk factors with a normal heart. Hypertrophy is structural disease, which puts him in stage B even without symptoms.
Stage C
Stage C requires past or current symptoms. He has never had any, so his hypertrophy places him in stage B.

set2.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set2.q: A 34-year-old woman has progressive leg edema and jugular venous distension (distended neck veins). At the apex there is a low-pitched diastolic rumble with an opening snap. Which is the most likely cause of her right-sided heart failure?
opts: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy leads the diastolic chain with a fourth heart sound. An apical diastolic rumble with a snap is mitral stenosis.
Mitral valve stenosis

Correct. A rumbling diastolic murmur at the apex with an opening snap is mitral stenosis, one of the three causes of right-sided failure with chronic left-sided failure and pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Tricuspid regurgitation
Tricuspid regurgitation gives a holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, louder on inspiration. An apical diastolic rumble with a snap is mitral stenosis.
Aortic valve stenosis
Aortic stenosis is the most common valvular cause of heart failure overall but does not give an apical diastolic rumble with a snap. This is mitral stenosis.

set2.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set2.q: A 65-year-old woman with heart failure has an echocardiogram reporting an ejection fraction of 44% and a multigated acquisition scan the same month reporting 32%. Which result should decide her ejection fraction group?
opts: Whichever value is higher
Choosing the higher value is not a rule. The multigated acquisition scan is the most accurate study for ejection fraction.
The multigated acquisition scan

Correct. The multigated acquisition scan is the most accurate study for ejection fraction, so its 32% places her in reduced ejection fraction. The echocardiogram is the one to trust for structures such as the valves.
The echocardiogram
The echocardiogram is most accurate for structures, not for ejection fraction. When the two disagree on the fraction, the multigated acquisition scan decides.
An average of the two
Averaging mixes a more accurate measure with a less accurate one. The multigated acquisition scan is the most accurate for ejection fraction.

set2.io: Compare and contrast precipitating factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis (including role of B-type natriuretic peptide, BNP), and treatment of acute decompensated heart failure.
set2.q: A 55-year-old man wore a defibrillator vest after an infarction while his guideline-directed therapy was optimized and he completed cardiac rehabilitation. His repeat echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 47%. Which is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Start inotropic therapy at home
Inotropes are for intensive care use only, and his heart has improved. He continues guideline-directed therapy without a device.
Continue therapy without a device
Correct. The implantable defibrillator is placed only if the repeat echocardiogram shows no improvement. At 47% his fraction is well above the 35% threshold, so therapy continues without a device.
Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator
The device requires an ejection fraction of 35% or less after optimized therapy. At 47% he no longer meets that.
Continue the vest indefinitely
The vest bridges the recovery period only. With his fraction recovered to 47%, he continues therapy without a device.

set2.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set2.q: A 54-year-old woman with pulmonary arterial hypertension has edema and distended neck veins. Her electrocardiogram shows right axis deviation, right bundle branch block and T-wave inversions in V1 to V3. What does this pattern indicate?
opts: Left ventricular hypertrophy
Hypertrophy shows tall R waves in V5 and V6 with deep S waves in V1 and V2. Her pattern is right heart strain.
Acute lateral infarction
Infarction shows ischemic changes in a coronary territory. Her pattern is right heart strain.
A normal variant tracing
This combination is not a normal variant; axis deviation, bundle branch block and inversions form the right heart strain pattern.
Right heart strain
Correct. Right axis deviation, right bundle branch block and T-wave inversions in V1 to V3 are the right heart strain pattern, fitting right-sided failure from pulmonary arterial hypertension.

set2.io: Define the following diagnostic and therapeutic groups of HF patients, and the treatment implications/recommendations for each group: a. HF with reduced EF (HFrEF) b. HF with mildly reduced EF (HFmrEF) c. HF with preserved EF (HFpEF)
set2.q: A 62-year-old woman is newly diagnosed with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (fraction 28%). She is breathless with ordinary exertion but comfortable at rest, and takes no renin-angiotensin drug. Which agent fits her symptom class?
opts: Dobutamine
Dobutamine is an inotrope for intensive care use only. Her class II reduced ejection fraction fits sacubitril-valsartan.
Metolazone alone
Metolazone is a thiazide-like diuretic used as needed for congestion, not renin-angiotensin therapy. Her class fits sacubitril-valsartan.
Sacubitril-valsartan
Correct. Symptoms with exertion are New York Heart Association class II, and the angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor is recommended for class II to III in reduced ejection fraction.
Diltiazem
Diltiazem is a calcium channel blocker, which is avoided in heart failure. Her class II reduced ejection fraction fits sacubitril-valsartan.

set2.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set2.q: A 67-year-old woman presents with fatigue, breathlessness with exertion and new ankle edema. Which blood test best supports a clinical diagnosis of heart failure?
opts: Serum potassium
Potassium is followed for therapy safety. The natriuretic peptide supports the diagnosis of heart failure.
B-type natriuretic peptide
Correct. Heart failure is a clinical diagnosis: signs and symptoms plus an elevated natriuretic peptide or objective congestion. The peptide is the laboratory test that carries that weight.
Complete blood count
The blood count helps with the differential, for example anemia, but does not support the diagnosis itself. The natriuretic peptide does.
Cardiac troponin
Troponin is ordered when infarction or ischemic cardiomyopathy is a concern. The natriuretic peptide supports the diagnosis of heart failure.

set2.io: Compare and contrast precipitating factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis (including role of B-type natriuretic peptide, BNP), and treatment of acute decompensated heart failure.
set2.q: A 57-year-old woman recovering from acute heart failure after an infarction, with an ejection fraction of 31%, asks why she must wear a defibrillator vest. Which explanation is accurate?
opts: It is permanent for everyone after infarction
The vest is a bridge. After optimized therapy and rehabilitation the echocardiogram is repeated to decide whether an implantable device is needed.
It measures her ejection fraction daily
The vest protects against sudden death; it does not measure function. The echocardiogram is repeated after optimized therapy.
It protects her while therapy is optimized

Correct. The vest covers the period in which guideline-directed therapy is optimized and she completes cardiac rehabilitation; the echocardiogram is then repeated to decide whether she needs an implantable device.
It replaces her heart failure medicines
The vest does not replace therapy; it protects her while therapy is optimized, before the echocardiogram is repeated.

set2.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set2.q: An 84-year-old woman with right-sided heart failure has progressive symptoms despite treatment of its cause and is not a transplant candidate. Which approach is most appropriate?
opts: Discharge without follow-up care
Withdrawing care is not the plan. Without a transplant option, palliative care focused on symptoms is the route.
Palliative care focused on symptoms

Correct. Right-sided failure is treated like left-sided failure, with symptom management, treatment of the cause, heart transplant or palliative care. When transplant is not an option, palliative care is the route.
Calcium channel blocker for comfort
Calcium channel blockers are avoided in heart failure. Without a transplant option, palliative care focused on symptoms is the route.
Inotropes started for home use
Inotropes are for intensive care use only. Without a transplant option, palliative care focused on symptoms is the route.

set2.io: Define the following diagnostic and therapeutic groups of HF patients, and the treatment implications/recommendations for each group: a. HF with reduced EF (HFrEF) b. HF with mildly reduced EF (HFmrEF) c. HF with preserved EF (HFpEF)
set2.q: A 69-year-old woman with mildly reduced ejection fraction (fraction 46%) is euvolemic on a diuretic. Which drug class is the next best-supported addition?
opts: Evidence-based beta blocker at once
In mildly reduced ejection fraction the beta blocker is only a weak recommendation. The sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor is better supported.
Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist
The antagonist is only a weak recommendation here. The sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor is better supported.
Diltiazem for rate and pressure
Diltiazem is a calcium channel blocker, avoided in heart failure. The next best-supported class is the sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor

Correct. After diuretics, the sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor carries a moderate recommendation in mildly reduced ejection fraction, ahead of the weak recommendations for the beta blocker, antagonist and renin-angiotensin drugs.

set2.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set2.q: A 64-year-old man with reduced ejection fraction (fraction 30%) on sacubitril-valsartan, a beta blocker, spironolactone and empagliflozin develops atrial fibrillation, and rate control is being planned. Which medication should be avoided?
opts: Diltiazem
Correct. Diltiazem is a calcium channel blocker, and calcium channel blockers are avoided in heart failure. His existing beta blocker belongs to core therapy.
Spironolactone
Spironolactone is a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, a strong recommendation in reduced ejection fraction. The drug to avoid is diltiazem.
Empagliflozin
Empagliflozin is a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, part of core therapy in reduced ejection fraction. The drug to avoid is diltiazem.
Sacubitril-valsartan
Sacubitril-valsartan is recommended in reduced ejection fraction for class II to III. The drug to avoid is diltiazem.

set2.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set2.q: A 70-year-old man with chronic left-sided heart failure develops right-sided failure. He asks what this means for his outlook. Which reply is accurate?
opts: It improves once edema clears
Clearing edema relieves symptoms but does not change the outlook: right-sided failure carries a much worse prognosis.
His prognosis is now much worse
Correct. Right-sided failure carries a much worse prognosis than left-sided failure, and in him it marks progression of chronic left-sided disease.
His prognosis is unchanged
The outlook does change: right-sided failure carries a much worse prognosis than left-sided failure.
His prognosis is now better
The comparison runs the other way. Right-sided failure carries a much worse prognosis than left-sided failure.

set2.io: Compare and contrast precipitating factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis (including role of B-type natriuretic peptide, BNP), and treatment of acute decompensated heart failure.
set2.q: A 66-year-old man has breathlessness, leg edema and a B-type natriuretic peptide of 280. Which study should come next to define his cardiac structure and ejection fraction?
opts: Right heart catheterization
Catheterization grades hemodynamic severity once right-sided failure is established. The first study for structure and ejection fraction is the echocardiogram.
Cardiac troponin level
Troponin looks for infarction or ischemic cardiomyopathy. The study that defines structure and ejection fraction is the echocardiogram.
Echocardiogram
Correct. An indeterminate peptide leaves the question open, and the echocardiogram shows structure most accurately and classifies heart failure by ejection fraction.
Repeat the peptide in a year
Waiting a year leaves a symptomatic patient undiagnosed. The echocardiogram defines structure and ejection fraction now.

set2.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set2.q: A 38-year-old woman with very heavy menstrual bleeding has fatigue, palpitations, ankle edema and a raised B-type natriuretic peptide. Echocardiogram is being arranged. Which additional test is most likely to identify the driver of her heart failure?
opts: Right heart catheterization
Catheterization grades hemodynamic severity in right-sided failure. The complete blood count identifies anemia, the likely driver here.
Chest radiograph
A radiograph can show congestion but not its cause. The complete blood count identifies anemia, the likely driver of high-output failure.
Complete blood count
Correct. Anemia is one of the causes of high-output failure, and the complete blood count is part of the high-output workup with the echocardiogram, metabolic panel and natriuretic peptide.
Cardiac troponin level
Troponin looks for infarction or ischemic cardiomyopathy, which nothing here suggests. The complete blood count looks for the anemia that heavy bleeding causes.

set2.io: Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing (including ordering and interpretation), management (acute and chronic, including applicable rehabilitative and palliative care), appropriate referrals, patient education, prevention, and prognosis for heart failure.
set2.q: A 45-year-old woman with a family history of heart failure smokes, drinks heavily and is obese. Her heart is structurally normal. Which counseling point best lowers her heart failure risk?
opts: Family history cannot be offset at all
Family history is fixed, but her modifiable risk factors (tobacco, alcohol, obesity) can still be changed to lower her risk.
Start a loop diuretic as prevention
Diuretics treat congestion and do not prevent heart failure. Counseling targets tobacco, alcohol and obesity.
Wait for symptoms before changing
Waiting forfeits prevention. Tobacco, excess alcohol and obesity are modifiable now.
Quit tobacco, cut alcohol, lose weight
Correct. Tobacco, excessive alcohol and obesity are modifiable risk factors for heart failure. Her family history is a risk factor she cannot change, so counseling targets the ones she can.

set2.io: Differentiate each stage of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA), natural history classification of heart failure, and associated treatment recommendations of each stage.
set2.q: A 57-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes has asymptomatic left ventricular hypertrophy on echocardiogram. She already takes an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor. Which drug class should be added for her diabetes-related risk?
opts: Angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor
The neprilysin combination belongs to symptomatic reduced ejection fraction in functional class II or III. Stage B with diabetes adds a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor
Correct. She is stage B, and stage B carries a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor for patients with diabetes as well as the converting enzyme inhibitor and a beta blocker.
Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist
The antagonist belongs to symptomatic heart failure. In stage B with diabetes the added class is the sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
Calcium channel blocker such as amlodipine
Calcium channel blockers are avoided in heart failure. In stage B with diabetes the added class is the sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
